title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two sisters from Rio Arriba County are suing the city of Española after a traffic stop on July 23. Jaclynn Gonzales, 21, was driving with her 12-year-old sister when a Flock Safety camera misread their license plate, confusing a final 2 for a 7 and matching a stolen car from Rio Rancho. Police stopped them on Calle Duran, handcuffed both, and placed them in separate patrol cars. Jaclynn asked an officer to call their mother, who lived nearby, to pick up the girl, but officers instead handcuffed the child and put her in another police vehicle.

The sisters filed separate lawsuits on January 3 in state District Court, seeking unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, worry, and restriction of movement. Their attorney, Sheri Raphaelson, also represents Adam Pacheco, a 17-year-old honor student who was forced to kneel after a similar mistaken alert in April. The city, Police Chief Mizel A. Garcia, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. The lawsuits are pending, and no next court date is mentioned.
